methods: Recovered the supplied images from the relocated OneDrive work/scan-images folder after the stale Codex-session paths failed.

Mapped each image filename prefix to the source-document SHA-256 prefix and the generating scan manifest, then reconciled the parent with the existing evidence catalogs, timeline sources and prior intake audits.

Ran local OCR on exactly the 309 supplied pages. Nineteen pages produced no machine text and were reviewed visually; they were blank or near-blank pages, tables, maps, covers, attachment placeholders or other image-dominant pages.
Excluded NPDES-petition pages 21 through 36 because they existed in the recovered working folder but were not included in the user's supplied page list.

Searched the supplied pages for Wexford, landfill, leachate, hauled waste, offloading, truck, gallons, delivery, manifests, load tickets, receiving logs, invoices, billing, payments, agreements, rate schedules, renewals, amendments and cessation evidence.
Compared the two rendered duplicate families byte-for-byte at the image level and suppressed derivative duplicates rather than creating new evidence records.

contentFindings.finding: The February 3, 2011 inspection history states that Cadillac's equalization tank accepted hauled waste described as landfill leachate from the County Landfill.
contentFindings.boundary: The same inspection statement says no screen or flow meter was apparent at that receiving area and provides no load date, time, hauler, actual gallons or receiving-log entry.

contentFindings.finding: The January 12, 2016 City letter records a 9:22 a.m. call from American Waste's leachate driver after an offloading spill and states that the tanker could hold up to 10,000 gallons.
contentFindings.boundary: The letter says only that less than the tanker capacity spilled. It is an incident report, not a manifest, receiving log or measured delivery record.

contentFindings.finding: The selected EM-Hauling pages are attachment wrappers, land-application field photographs and biosolids laboratory-report pages.
contentFindings.boundary: They concern outbound biosolids hauling and do not document inbound Wexford landfill-leachate deliveries.

contentFindings.finding: The supplied terminal pages preserve chain-of-custody and sample-receipt material for the October 2018 leachate sample.
contentFindings.boundary: They document laboratory custody, not a landfill-to-WWTP delivery transaction or cessation date.

queueDecision: No receiving-history requirement is closed. The supplied page renders contain no per-load manifest or ticket, WWTP receiving log, delivery-linked invoice or ledger, fully executed 2009 agreement with signed rate schedule, signed renewal or amendment, or dated final-delivery record.
evidentiaryBoundary: The batch corroborates the receiving point, the absence of an apparent flow meter in the 2011 inspection history and the documented 2016 offloading spill. It cannot be converted into a load-by-load delivery series, executed contract record or precise cessation date. Page renders remain derivatives of their parent records and were not added as separate primary documents.
